reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive multisystem disorder whose hallmark is cryptophthalmos, in which skin covers one or both eyes with absent or fused eyelids
Cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers and toes is a characteristic and readily recognised feature
Genitourinary anomalies are frequent and include renal agenesis and ambiguous genitalia
Laryngeal and airway malformations may cause severe neonatal respiratory obstruction
The combination of bilateral renal agenesis and laryngeal atresia contributes to high perinatal mortality
It is caused by variants in genes of the FRAS-FREM complex, which anchor the embryonic epidermis to the underlying basement membrane
Diagnostic criteria weigh major features such as cryptophthalmos, syndactyly, and genital and renal anomalies against minor features
reference.pathophysiology: Fraser syndrome is caused by autosomal recessive loss-of-function variants in genes encoding components of the FRAS-FREM protein complex, which forms part of the basement membrane and mediates adhesion between the developing epidermis and dermis during embryogenesis. Failure of this adhesion disturbs the normal separation and modelling of tissues, so structures that should divide or open do not, producing cryptophthalmos from failed eyelid separation, cutaneous syndactyly from failed digital separation, and blockage of the larynx and urinary tract. Because these adhesion proteins act at multiple epithelial-mesenchymal interfaces during development, the disorder affects the eyes, digits, airway, and genitourinary system together.
additionalDifferentials: Bilateral renal agenesis (Potter) sequence from other causes
Bartsocas-Papas and other lethal syndactyly syndromes
Amniotic band sequence affecting the eyes and digits
additionalInvestigations: Antenatal ultrasound, which may show renal anomalies, oligohydramnios, and other features
Molecular testing of FRAS-FREM complex genes
Airway endoscopy to assess laryngeal patency in the neonate
Ophthalmological and orbital imaging to define the ocular anomaly
Radiographs and examination to characterise syndactyly and skeletal anomalies
redFlags: Neonatal airway obstruction from laryngeal atresia or stenosis requiring immediate intervention
Bilateral renal agenesis, which is incompatible with survival
Undiagnosed urinary tract obstruction threatening kidney function
Ambiguous genitalia requiring careful multidisciplinary evaluation
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is heavily determined by the airway and renal anomalies; bilateral renal agenesis or laryngeal atresia often results in perinatal death, whereas survivors with preserved renal and airway function can do reasonably well with staged reconstruction.
pitfalls: Overlooking life-threatening laryngeal atresia while attention focuses on the visible eye defect
Failing to assess renal function early given the high frequency of renal agenesis
Missing the diagnosis when cryptophthalmos is incomplete or unilateral
Not recognising the autosomal recessive recurrence risk for counselling
Attributing the presentation to amniotic band sequence and missing the underlying genetic disorder
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
GeneReviews and Gorlin's Syndromes of the Head and Neck
